methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort of 189 HER2-positive BC patients with pathologically confirmed nodal metastasis. LASSO regression with 10-fold cross-validation for feature selection, multivariable logistic regression for model construction. Events-per-variable ratio approximately 38 indicating low overfitting risk. Internal validation by 1000 bootstrap resamples. Limitations: single-center, retrospective design; 5.8% missing axillary data imputed using median.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study (LoE 2b) with direct clinical relevance to axillary de-escalation surgery in HER2-positive breast cancer. Nomogram predicts axillary pathological complete response (apCR), a key endpoint for minimally invasive axillary approaches (SLNB, targeted axillary dissection). Confirmed prognostic value of apCR (HR=0.29, DFS benefit). Addresses unmet preoperative decision-making need.

reporting_quality.justification: Prediction model study following TRIPOD reporting standards with clear patient selection, variable definitions (HR status, HER2 IHC/FISH criteria per standard), treatment classification (single vs dual anti-HER2), imaging response assessment blinded to treatment, statistical methods detailed (R packages specified). Comprehensive outcome definitions (apCR, bpCR, DFS). No data/code repository statement.

novelty_literature.justification: Nomogram predicting apCR in HER2-positive BC using three integrated clinical variables (baseline axillary burden, early ultrasound response, anti-HER2 intensity). Addresses cited gap: prior models use postoperative parameters (bpCR) or heterogeneous cohorts. However, incremental contribution building on established concepts (imaging response, treatment intensity, baseline tumor burden).

writing_presentation.justification: Well-written with clear clinical problem statement, detailed methods including imaging protocol (radiologist blinded, >5 years experience), statistical approach transparent, results presented with appropriate figures (ROC, calibration, DCA, CIC, Kaplan-Meier). Discussion mechanistically grounds findings in HER2 biology and circulating tumor DNA literature.

key_strengths: Addresses genuine clinical need: preoperative prediction of axillary pCR to guide de-escalation surgery (SLNB vs TAD vs ALND) in HER2-positive BC

Robust statistical approach: LASSO regression with 10-fold cross-validation for feature selection; multivariable logistic regression with events-per-variable ratio ~38; internal validation by 1000 bootstrap resamples
Three readily available preoperative predictors (baseline axillary burden, early ultrasound response, anti-HER2 therapy intensity) with biological plausibility and clinical actionability
Comprehensive model validation: AUC 0.735 with robust calibration; DCA and CIC demonstrate clinical utility across probability thresholds
Confirmed prognostic value of apCR as surrogate for improved DFS (HR=0.29, 3-year rate 95.4% vs 86.6%; P=0.036)
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective cohort (n=189) limiting external generalizability; no external validation provided in independent cohort
Moderate discriminative ability (AUC 0.735) suggests modest predictive accuracy; calibrated AUC from bootstrap validation (0.708) slightly lower

Differential follow-up between groups (apCR 32 months vs non-apCR 40 months) may introduce ascertainment bias; conservative truncation at July 2022 for lost patients acknowledges but doesn't fully mitigate this
bpCR deliberately excluded from preoperative model citing lack of routine minimally invasive biopsy; however, this limits model discrimination and ignores available patients with tissue diagnosis
No data/code availability statement; reproducibility outside institutional setting unclear
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically sound prediction model study with clinical relevance and confirmed prognostic value. Single-center retrospective design and moderate AUC (0.735) appropriate for Tier 2 (10-19 JIF) with minor revisions emphasizing need for prospective external validation before clinical implementation.
